answer: One horn blast across a canyon buys a seat, but only if two knolls hear it the same way: at first light over the tundra, a newcomer sounds one horn from the rim while two listeners on neighbouring knolls time the echo against the surveyed width. An echo off by more than half a second, or a listener who never logs, voids the claim and burns a 500 POA bond. Each sounding costs $140 for the horn plus $60 per listener, so 100 fakes need 100 soundings, $26,000 in fees and 50,000 POA in bonds.
